title: Turn a Django detail view's 500 into a 404 with get_object_or_404
summary: A detail view answers 500 for a missing pk. Swap in get_object_or_404, then hide drafts behind the same 404.

files.content:
from django.db import models


class Article(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    body = models.TextField()
    is_published = models.BooleanField(default=False)

turns.user: /articles/999/ gives a 500. should obviously be a 404 if it doesn't exist

assistant.body: Good catch! Article.objects.get raises Article.DoesNotExist when no row matches. Nothing in the view catches it, so Django turns it into a 500. get_object_or_404 from django.shortcuts raises Http404 instead, and Django answers that with a 404.

turns.user: oh and drafts show up if you type the url directly. published only

assistant.body: Sure. get_object_or_404 takes the same keyword arguments as filter, so adding is_published=True is all it needs. In other words, a draft now gets the same 404 as an article that does not exist. It is not a 403, so nobody outside can tell that the draft is there.
